superseded_plan.content:
# Babylon visual rebuild

Owner direction, 2026-10-24: replace flat illustrated actors and placeholder scenery with actual modeled characters and a finished arena. Babylon.js drives character animation and ability effects. Existing 2D pictures serve as reference for shape, costume, palette and mood; they are not the finished world objects.

This is the single active visual production plan. Earlier sprite, migration and avatar-finishing directions are historical. `/root` owns this plan and documentation reset; no delegates. **Status: planning and current-code inventory complete; new geometry, rigs and animations have not been implemented.** Nothing is visually qualified by this document. Runtime remains the existing presentation until phased replacements are implemented and verified.

## What we are making

A cohesive stylized 3D arena at the current spectator camera: recognizable modeled faces, bodies, clothes, equipment and species; genuine turning and limb motion; substantial towers and monsters; geometry-based scenery; character-specific effects. Strong silhouettes and material contrast take priority over tiny detail. Simple primitive blockouts are construction aids, never the final character or tower deliverable. Forty-five recolored copies of one mannequin do not satisfy the roster.

Author custom surfaces in TypeScript using Babylon mesh/vertex geometry, with reusable modeling tools for lofts, bevels, profiles and layered cloth. Use skeletal deformation where surfaces must bend and articulated TransformNode hierarchies for rigid equipment and appropriate mechanical parts. Use Babylon animation tracks/groups and deterministic snapshot-time sampling; procedural secondary motion is an accent, not a substitute for walking or casting. A later imported asset must meet the same gates; no external model generator or failed historical GLB is assumed as a dependency.

The 2D avatar and ability PNGs and environment concepts remain reference artifacts, outside the final world-rendering path. Normal material textures may support modeled surfaces, but a whole character, tree or arena painting on a plane cannot substitute for geometry. Existing interface portraits/icons are outside the world-model replacement scope; they must not become floating ability illustrations. No new illustration generation is needed to begin.

## Non-negotiable boundaries

- Preserve current avatar IDs, original identities, body plans, handedness, companions, equipment and kit definitions. Canonical sources: `EsportsClash.Web/src/data/heroIdentityV3.json`, `src/data/v3RosterDesign.json`, actual catalog and executable V3 handlers. Existing drawings inform appearance, not mechanics. Resolve any anatomy conflict between a drawing and the current anatomy registry explicitly before building that avatar.
- Follow `docs/character-asset-pipeline.md`: clean adult anatomy-appropriate neutral base, verified rig and controlled bends first, then costume/weapon/hair fitting. Nonhumanoids retain their actual anatomy. Raw/base, rig, appearance and motion outputs are separate stages even when authored in code. The existing failed Mirelle candidate remains unqualified and unpublished; do not fit clothes over its failures or restore deleted binaries.
- Retain the current 2600 by 1440 map, lane and camp/brush/rock/structure coordinates, terrain legality and camera projection. Rebuild the visual treatment without moving gameplay objects or restoring the discarded simplified map. Geometry must follow authoritative positions; decoration cannot invent collision or vision.
- Rendering consumes copied match state and actual release/commit/hit/destroy events. No invented hits, altered damage, clock/RNG draws, strategic fallback, cooldown or AI changes. Tower damage/attribution, all-three-barracks order, aliases and frozen ML artifacts remain protected.
- Separate visible completion from structural validity. Preserve failed candidates and evidence; record source/artifact hashes and owner/stage in each handoff. No blanket publication or full-roster qualification from one passing example.

## Phase 0 ? Reset and inventory

**Completed for this planning pass.** Removed five superseded generated planning/reference Markdown guides; exact content and SHA-256 are retained in `visual-reset-20261024.json`. Supplied specifications, historical implementation/verification reports, asset-reset/deformation records, pictures, manifests, logs and gameplay/ML documentation are retained. Older reports describe their original results, not the new direction.

Current code inventory:

| Existing area | Problem / intended replacement |
| --- | --- |
| `match-viewer/BabylonMatchViewer.ts` | `ensureActor` selects `PaintedRoster` before the model loader. Replace with explicit per-avatar 3D factory once the new character passes its gate. |
| `PaintedRoster.ts`, `illustrationMotion.ts` | Billboard character plus whole-image motion. Retire from the final arena after the corresponding modeled character is ready. |
| `PaintedAbilities.ts` | Floating illustrated tokens. Replace with actual modeled devices, trails, particles and readable warning/impact choreography. |
| `BabylonBattlefield.ts` | Simple cylinders/polyhedra form towers, minions and other actors. Replace by dedicated builders, not more ornaments around the same proxies. |
| `PaintedArena.ts`, `PaintedScenery.ts`, `PaintedBackdrop.ts` | Composited painting and cutout scenery. Replace with terrain materials, modeled props and a coherent geometric horizon. |
| `AbilityWorldEffects.ts`, `abilityEffectPlan.ts` | Reusable event-driven plumbing exists. Retain useful state/resource handling; generic beams/rings are not finished per-kit VFX. |
| `ArenaFrame.ts`, `MatchViewer.ts`, `ViewerReplay.ts` | Retain the read-only boundary and replay. Add only the visual facts needed for real sockets, phases and effect ownership. |
| `BabylonAssets.ts`, `AvatarAnimationController.ts` | Inspect and reuse useful lifecycle/animation logic. Do not reactivate deleted releases or treat old clip-name checks as animation qualification. |

**Exit:** one current plan, explicit inventory and preserved evidence. Completed; no runtime reset or new model delivery is claimed.

## Phase 1 ? Establish the 3D visual foundation

Build a small Babylon inspection scene using the actual match camera, lighting, ground-height convention and actor scale. Include front/side/rear/orbit inspection, reference beside the model, wireframe/joints, paused poses and exact-time scrubbing. Establish material language for stone, skin, cloth, metal and restrained emissive accents. Tune lighting and contact shadows around real volumes rather than baked painted shadows.

Create a shared custom-mesh toolkit and explicit geometry/material disposal ownership. Establish a provisional 60 fps desktop / 30 fps mobile frame-time target, then measure named devices before assigning triangle, shadow, draw-call and effect budgets. Those are goals, not measured claims. Load only selected-match characters.

**Exit:** a representative sculpted prop and anatomical body study read clearly at normal match zoom and close-up, with no billboard substitution; initial measured cost is recorded. No full arena rollout yet.

## Phase 2 ? Mirelle anatomy and articulation

Mirelle (`c_invoker`) is the first character, matching the fresh-start order. Author a new clean base with readable face/head, separated hands/fingers and appropriate proportions in the required wide neutral A-pose. Construct proper local joint axes, shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees and ankles; use skinned surfaces where necessary rather than visible stacks of disconnected tubes. Save raw base and rig stages separately.

Validate isolated bend/twist poses before clothing: planted feet, shoulder clearance, hand/hip separation, finite transforms, weights where used, surface collisions and stretch across motion. Inspect actual Babylon-rendered geometry from multiple angles. Compare stage outputs to find the first defect instead of smoothing every weight or hiding the joint.

**Exit:** visually acceptable neutral anatomy and controlled deformation. The existing failed Mirelle GLB cannot count as passing this phase.

## Phase 3 ? Finish one playable character and one arena section

Fit Mirelle's identity after Phase 2 passes: modeled hair, ivory waistcoat, asymmetrical dark sleeve, oxblood skirt over shorts, flat boots, pattern cape, needle comb and a recognizable brass bobbin. Model equipment grips and sockets; make cloth/accessories follow their correct joints. Inspect the full silhouette, face, materials, handedness and costume from every playable angle.

Author Idle, Walk, Run, Turn, Basic Attack, S1, S2, Ultimate, Hit, Death and Spawn/Respawn motion, with distinct skill gestures and actual anticipation/release/recovery. Movement uses real speed and direction with grounded contacts; attacks honor release time; Death reaches the floor and holds. Blend interruptions without resetting locomotion or implying control effects. Playback must agree at pause, seek and 1x/2x/4x.

Build one **finished tower and lane/jungle edge segment** in the same style: shaped masonry, plinth, articulated firing/emissive element, damage/destruction state, paving depth, cliff/soil transitions, modeled vegetation and clean ground contact. This is the visual benchmark for the rest of the arena; cylinders and picture cutouts do not pass as final props.

**Exit:** a short actual-match demonstration with the finished Mirelle, movement/attack/cast/death/respawn, the tower and lane section. Inspect close-up, normal spectator zoom and crowded combat scale. Do not multiply an unsatisfactory prototype across 45 avatars.

## Phase 4 ? Finish Mirelle's ability choreography

Replace atlas symbols with authored Babylon geometry, particles, trails, materials and timed animation. Every ability has a source gesture/socket, a warning where the mechanic has one, an active object/effect, a confirmed impact and an expiry/destruction transition. Use actual pins and thread; no generic elemental orb replacement. Cover passive pin state, S1, Recut and all ten ultimate patterns individually.

Render attackable objects as recognizable objects with state/lifetime cues. Warning, active, disabled, interrupted and expired states must differ; retain safe gaps and actual endpoints. Ground markings remain functional aids, never the entire ability. Review lighting/opacity so effects neither disappear against stone nor obscure ten combatants.

**Exit:** one end-to-end character with all kit states in a real match and replay. No phantom impact on a miss/blocked cast, no warning after expiry, and exact hit/safe-area geometry. Per-pattern evidence is required, not just a shared color theme.

## Phase 5 ? Replace the arena's remaining placeholders

Extend the approved tower/lane style to both bases and all structure types, distinct barracks, Nexus, wells, minion classes, wards, neutral camps, bosses, rocks, bushes, trees, cliffs, river/ground transitions and distant surroundings. Inventory every world object as `placeholder`, `modeled`, `animated`, `verified` or `complete`; attach evidence to each completed type.

Use instancing/material sharing for repeated geometry. Keep traversable surfaces and actual blockers visually consistent with mechanics; add no new terrain rules. Distinguish targetable creatures/structures from decorative objects. Include spawning, attacks, taking damage, destruction and held dead/respawn states where applicable. Reduce occluding foliage near combat without flattening the forest into cutout pictures.

**Exit:** an actual 5v5 match camera traversal has no unintended proxy towers, primitive mobs, cutout trees, pasted paving seams or empty backdrop boundaries. Arena art is coherent at all camera limits and viewport sizes. Mixed old/new scenery is temporary phase work, never final acceptance.

## Phase 6 ? Expand from Mirelle to all 45

Before mass production, finish two additional body-plan proofs: a creature/nonhumanoid and a companion/rider/vehicle identity selected from the actual roster. Confirm species-specific locomotion, independent companion motion and suitable rest rigs. Reuse modeling tools and rig families only where anatomy permits; preserve individual silhouette, face, weapons, posture and kit choreography.

Then complete the remaining **42 avatars in batches of six**. Each of seven batches includes model, anatomy gate, dressed deformation, full motion set, all four ability slots, actual-match integration and evidence. A roster tracker lists all 45 stable IDs and each gate separately; it must not label an entire batch complete because files load. Do not author all bodies first while leaving every character without a finished kit.

**Exit per avatar:** recognizable modeled identity at match zoom; correct facing/weapon contacts/locomotion/death; all actual kit states; replay correctness; documented resource use and no unresolved blocking deformation defect. **Exit phase:** 45 individually verified characters, not 45 material variants.

## Phase 7 ? Integrate, remove temporary paths and qualify

Move completed factories into the default Babylon match/replay path in verified increments. Remove `PaintedRoster`/illustration animation and `PaintedAbilities` from the finished world path; retire painted scenery/backdrop compositing once modeled replacements pass. Keep reference files and historical evidence outside runtime dependencies. Verify that a qualified 3D actor cannot silently fall back to a picture. A graphics failure should be explicit rather than presenting an unfinished proxy as the completed asset.

Verify ten independently animated champions, waves, all structures and simultaneous effects in a natural match. Check target visibility, depth/transparency, occlusion, reduced motion, graphics/context recovery, lifecycle cleanup, asset loading, pause/seek/replay and device frame-time/memory budgets. Run `npm run check:game` and `npm run build` after integration changes; compare authoritative state/RNG where renderer changes could affect the boundary. Update both handoff and mechanics with evidence and remaining limits.

**Exit:** no sprite actors or unintentional placeholder world objects in the finished arena; all 45 pass the tracker; per-kit ability review and an uninterrupted natural-match review are recorded; performance is measured on named devices. Release qualification follows existing controls. No promise of a professional-quality finished roster from a build/test pass alone.

## Immediate next work

Phase 1 is next: build the isolated Babylon modeling/animation inspection scene and establish custom geometry, materials, grounding and measurable costs. Then complete Mirelle's new anatomy/rig before adding her outfit. The first reviewable milestone is **one finished moving Mirelle plus one finished tower/lane section**, followed by her complete kit. Completion evidence is an actual rendered motion demonstration, not another illustrated mockup or plan.
